title: I1-phase-session-folder-directive.md.txt
body:
# Phase directive — «Session folder trusted by viola» (Epoch 4's head entry, viola-0.2.0, v2-33)

1. Scope is the route entry and its carry as they stand at `c2310c28`, nothing wider: a session viola starts in a
   folder the CLI never trusted opens with no trust dialog and no key typed by viola.
2. **The founder's ruling on HOW is in the carry, and its ORDER binds the phase:** FIRST measure whether the CLI has
   a flag or a setting that trusts a folder; if one exists, viola uses it. ONLY if none does, viola writes
   `projects[cwd].hasTrustDialogAccepted` into the user's `~/.claude.json`. So P3 measures before P4 chooses:
   - from the installed CLI itself, with no live start: its `--help` and every subcommand's, the settings schema
     and the strings of the 2.1.325 bundle (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude`) and of 2.1.326 —
     any flag, setting, environment key or managed-settings field that makes a folder trusted or skips the trust
     dialog; for each candidate say what it does BEYOND trust (a flag that also skips permission prompts is not a
     trust flag, and using it is a widening of its own — name it, do not take it);
   - what `projects[cwd]` holds beside `hasTrustDialogAccepted`, and which process writes that file when (measured
     2026-11-17: the host's other Claude sessions rewrite `~/.claude.json` about once a minute — a writer that
     reads, edits and writes it races them; say how the write is made so no other session's write is lost and
     none of ours is, or that it cannot be and what follows).
3. **Writing the CLI's own state file is a boundary widening, named so in the carry**, and takes its security-plan
   entry. The plan lists it as an Expected amendment; its exact bound (which key, which cwd, when, never another
   project's entry, what viola does when the file is absent, unreadable, a link, or not the JSON it expects, and
   that nothing of the file is logged) is put to the founder through the overseer at P3's end, in the block below
   — do not settle it yourself.
4. **SIZE and the live starts FIRST.** At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block:
   (a) what the measurement found — each candidate, what it does, and which arm of the ruling it selects;
   (b) whether the chunk fits one implement window (say your own window at that point), and a split named plainly
   if not — the placement is the founder's;
   (c) the live starts on the standing rig: for each the SHAPE first (the cwd and its trust state, what makes the
   dialog appear or not, what the start reads if the mechanism failed and the dialog DOES stand), then the exact
   count per CLI version (2.1.325 by path; PATH's 2.1.326 is unstamped — say whether this reading needs it), and
   **every byte the rig types, the STOP included**: the keys into a dialog or a box (granted anew per chunk) apart
   from the stop (Ctrl-C into the rig's own pty, or a no-key group kill — standing, per the re-worded
   `security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty`). The summary's `keys:` word names the argv grant only;
   the block names both.
   (d) what viola's write does to the founder's REAL config during a live start, if a start exercises it: the rig
   runs under a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so say which file the product writes there and that his real file is
   read only by the mark witness.
   The cap, the keys and the bound of item 3 are the founder's; the overseer brings them to him in one dialog.
   Plan every other step on the fake agent meanwhile.
5. No mutation run. Name each control's `--timeout S` in the plan's prose AND fire it with that flag, on an entry
   whose build reaches every binary its case needs; a control id — and a sweep pattern id — stays within 16
   characters; «holds» = those cases ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Every acceptance predicate is one that
   CAN fail: for each control say what the subject does when the guard is gone, measured or marked unmeasured.
6. A change to the fake agent's screens puts `cli_verify` in the gate block. A test that waits takes a bound under
   the 20 s lint. A gate entry that names an installed tool's path is checked against the host before the card.
7. A fold is decided at the PHASE. If implement meets a red that moves a plan entry it stops and says so BEFORE the
   operator pass.
8. A fork that is the founder's (a boundary widening, a live cap, a typed key, a placement) is asked through the
   overseer, who brings it to him by dialog — he is present, slow to answer; a technical fork is answered by relay
   at once.
9. Set NO scheduled wake or timer of your own. End every process you start.
10. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; rows read whole or by search; whether EVERY cited row is in
    the union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` /
    `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

title: The measurement (directive item 2) — from the installed CLI, no live start

data.head: ## The measurement (directive item 2) — from the installed CLI, no live start

body:
Read from the bundles' strings (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude`, 365 842 960 B, and
`…/2.1.326/claude`, 371 429 904 B), by `strings -n 8` and a byte-offset context reader
(`scratchpad/ctx.py <bundle> <needle> <before> <after>`); no `claude` process was started.
**Candidates — what each does, and the ruling's arm it selects:**

1. `--trust-workspace` — «Trust the current folder for this run only, without asking (for scripts and CI)». Registered
   on the `ultrareview` subcommand only (2.1.325: the option chain after `--post` / `--no-post`; 2.1.326 the same, and
   the CLI's own `ultrareview … --no-post --trust-workspace --json` spawn); the self-hosted runner reads its own
   `--trust-workspace` / `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_TRUST_WORKSPACE` and SEEDS persisted trust by writing
   `projects[<path>] = {hasTrustDialogAccepted: true}` into `<configDir>/.claude.json` at mode 0600 (384). Not an
   option of the interactive session viola starts → no flag arm.

2. `--trusted-folder <absolute>` — «The current directory, which the host says a person trusted»: an option of the
   hidden `worktree-hook` subcommand (Claude Desktop's WorktreeCreate/Remove hooks) only → no flag arm.

3. `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED` (env) — the trust check returns trusted at once (`if(i.CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED)return!0`,
   2.1.325 `SL()`, 2.1.326 `OU()`), and BEYOND trust it switches off the project-permission gate (`wDo()` returns
   true → the gated project grants are not probed) and gives the `sandboxed` verdict to workspace checks: it is no
   trust flag but a sandbox posture — a widening of its own, named, not taken.
4. `CLAUDE_CODE_IGNORE_PERSISTED_TRUST` / `--ignore-persisted-trust` — the opposite: no trust record counts.

5. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` / `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` / `--permission-mode` — permission
   bypass, no trust: not candidates.

6. No settings-schema key and no managed-settings field trusts a folder: the settings literals near the trust code
   are `additionalDirectories` (permission scope, no trust) and `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt` (bypass-mode
   prompt); the trust state lives only in the global config's `projects` map.
**→ No flag, setting, env key or managed field trusts a folder for an interactive session without doing more. The
ruling's second arm stands: the per-project trust record.**

**The record — how the CLI reads it (2.1.325 `SL()`; 2.1.326 `OU()`, the same body):** trusted when
`CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED`; else when this session already accepted; else when
`projects[<project key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted` is true, the project key `f0e()` = the cwd's git root when the cwd
is in a git repository, else the normalised cwd; else by a walk from the cwd up to the git root (`bS` → `SS`), any
folder on the way whose record is true trusting it — save a `rootOnly` branch (`M2o`: a root whose `Lzo(root)` is not
true) where only the root's record counts. **Unmeasured:** what `Lzo` decides (the `rootOnly` branch's condition).
The home folder's trust is never recorded (session-only).

**The record — how the CLI writes it:** `ES(key)` → `{...config, projects: {...projects, [key]: {...projects[key] ??
ETe, hasTrustDialogAccepted: true}}}`, key `fD(cwd)` = the git root (canonical) or the cwd; `ETe`, a new project's
defaults: `allowedTools: []`, `mcpContextUris: []`, `mcpServers: {}`, `enabledMcpjsonServers: []`,
`disabledMcpjsonServers: []`, `hasTrustDialogAccepted: false`, `hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesApproved: false`,
`hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesWarningShown: false`. The CLI's own messages name the record as the user's remedy:
«…or set projects[<path>].hasTrustDialogAccepted: true in <config path>» (`Vj()` = the global config file).

**Who writes the file, and how (the race, directive item 2's second half):** every CLI save (`_p`) applies its
updater function to the config as it reads it at the save, merging `projects` (`zi(v.projects, k.projects)`), and
watches the file for other processes (`fs.watchFile` / a storage interface); a lock `<config>.lock` (proper-lockfile's
directory form, `lockfilePath: \`${e}.lock\``, retries 5·10·20·40·80 ms) is taken only when the feature gate
`tengu_swift_glade` is on (`Jf()`; off → no lock). So a key viola adds survives a later CLI save that reads after
viola's write; it is lost only when a CLI process read the file before viola's replace and writes after it (the
read-modify-write window), and no lock viola could take excludes a CLI process whose gate is off. **Lean:** take the
CLI's own lock directory when it can be had (cooperating with every CLI whose gate is on), replace the file atomically
(a temp file in the same directory, renamed), then read it back before the spawn and retry a bounded number of times
if the record is gone; a record still lost at the spawn leaves the dialog standing for the human (viola types
nothing), and the start reads it as a modal. Whether the bound and this form are taken is the founder's (directive
item 3).

**Which file the child reads:** the CLI's global config is `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json` when that variable is
set, else `~/.claude.json` (witness: the rig's `seed_config` writes `<config>/.claude.json` with a trust record and
passes `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<config>` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:150,221-232` — and its trusted starts open
with no dialog). viola's R8 strip removes `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` from the child unless `config.json`'s `claude_env_keep`
names it (`src/run/env.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:271-274`), and viola reads names only, never a
value (`src/run/env.rs:1-2`). So the file viola must write is `~/.claude.json` when the name is not kept, and the kept
value's `.claude.json` when it is — the second a new env VALUE read (a bound question).

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` (140-260) — the rig's private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `claude_env_keep`, and
  `seed_config(trusted)` writing the trust record into the PRIVATE config.
- `src/run/env.rs` (1-80) — `claude_env_keep`: names only, at most 32, `^CLAUDE…`.

- `src/cmd/run.rs` (156-395) — `start`: program resolution, collision, pin + plugin, the strip plan and the version
  gate (`:288-289`), bind, state, then `spawn_child` (`:372`), shared by `run` and `revive`.
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` (265-300) — home resolution through `std::env::home_dir()` (`HOME`).
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` (pub items) — `Gate { cli_version, cli_verified }`.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` (1-140) — `LedgerRow`, 22 variants relied (`relied()`).
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs` (20-60) — Run A `untrusted_run`: a fresh OS-temp dir, the settled modal, a kill.

- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` (100-190, 910-1010) — trust decided by argv `--trusted-root` (`trusted()`), the
  2.1.325 unnumbered trust form drawn under `--screens`.
- `tests/support/home.rs` (690-710) — `Wrapper::boot_untrusted` / `boot_in`.
- `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` — whole.
- the report fact `fct-ygdko332` (chunk 2026-11-15-live-round-on-the-trimmed-product, Addendum 2) — entry 27's record.
- the sealed relay `2026-11-15T18-01-44-wrap/inputs/I1-e2-0.2.0-route-adaptation.md.txt` — item C, the anchors.
- the two CLI bundles (strings; read-only).

- **start** (`src/cmd/run.rs`) — 3 callers: `cmd/run/run()` at `src/cmd/run.rs:187`, `cmd/revive/started()` at
  `src/cmd/revive.rs:154`, the span test at `src/cmd/run.rs:1316` (trace `tree-query-{marker}.json`, query 1) — one
  site serves both start arms.

- **version_gate** — called once in product code, `cmd/run/start()` at `src/cmd/run.rs:289`, plus its unit test
  `src/run/version_gate.rs:465`.

- trust symbols (query 4, `name LIKE '%trust%'`): the rig's screen/keys (viola-e2e), the fake's `Opts#trusted_root`
  / `trusted()` / `draw_trust()`, verify's `untrusted_run()` / `trusted_run()` / `Inputs#trusted`, `tests/cli_send.rs`
  `send_on_a_verified_cli_refuses_while_the_trust_dialog_is_up`; no product symbol writes a trust record.

- **Write after the gate, before the spawn** (`src/cmd/run.rs:288-372`): every start decision that depends on the
  CLI's verified behaviour reads `gate.cli_verified`; the spawn is last.

- **Claude shapes in one crate** (arch `decision/agent-claude-pure`): the key names (`projects`,
  `hasTrustDialogAccepted`) and the record's edit as a pure function over a JSON value belong in
  `viola-agent-claude`; the file's lock, bounded read and replace in the root bin (the crate does no file I/O).

- **A relied CLI behaviour is a ledger row with a verify probe** (arch `decision/capability-ledger-gate`): the CLI
  honouring a record another process wrote is undocumented → a 23rd relied row; every stamp of an older row set reads
  unverified (`decision/version-verified-all-relied-rows`).

- **Verify's untrusted run** (`runs.rs:26-38`): a fresh OS-temp dir, the first settled screen, a kill — the probe's
  natural twin is the same run with the record written for its dir, reading the input box instead of the modal.

- **Bounded reads** (security.md Session Addition 2026-11-16): `take(reader, MAX_FRAME).read_to_end(…)`, the
  `contract_bounded_readers` census.

- **Codes-only errors and the NEVER-log floor**: nothing of the CLI's config (a key, a path, a value) reaches a log
  line, event, reply or error; `thiserror` messages interpolate nothing (`tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`).
- **A waiting test bounded under the 20 s lint**; a fake-agent screen change puts `cli_verify` in the gate block.

- `src/run/trust.rs` — the trust record's write at the start: the config file's path, the CLI's lock, the bounded
  read, the agent crate's pure edit, the atomic replace and the read-back.

- `tests/cli_run_trust.rs` — e2e cases: an untrusted folder opens at the box with no dialog and no key; other
  projects' entries unchanged byte for byte; the refusing forms (absent / unreadable / link / not JSON).
- `src/cmd/run.rs` — call the trust write in `start` between the version gate and the spawn.
- `src/run/mod.rs` — declare `trust`.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — the 23rd relied row and its probe check.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — the record's pure edit and key literals, re-exported.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` — `relied.len()` 22 → 23.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_runs.rs` — the probe run's cases.

title: The measurement (directive item 2) — from the installed CLI, no live start

data.head: ## The measurement (directive item 2) — from the installed CLI, no live start

body:
**Which file the child reads:** the CLI's global config is `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json` when that variable is
set, else `~/.claude.json` (witness: the rig's `seed_config` writes `<config>/.claude.json` with a trust record and
passes `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<config>` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:150,221-232` — and its trusted starts open
with no dialog). viola's R8 strip removes `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` from the child unless `config.json`'s `claude_env_keep`
names it (`src/run/env.rs`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:271-274`), and viola reads names only, never a
value (`src/run/env.rs:1-2`). So the file viola must write is `~/.claude.json` when the name is not kept, and the kept
value's `.claude.json` when it is — the second a new env VALUE read (a bound question).

**Who writes the file, and how (the race, directive item 2's second half):** every CLI save (`_p`) applies its
updater function to the config as it reads it at the save, merging `projects` (`zi(v.projects, k.projects)`), and
watches the file for other processes (`fs.watchFile` / a storage interface); a lock `<config>.lock` (proper-lockfile's
directory form, `lockfilePath: \`${e}.lock\``, retries 5·10·20·40·80 ms) is taken only when the feature gate
`tengu_swift_glade` is on (`Jf()`; off → no lock). So a key viola adds survives a later CLI save that reads after
viola's write; it is lost only when a CLI process read the file before viola's replace and writes after it (the
read-modify-write window), and no lock viola could take excludes a CLI process whose gate is off. **Lean:** take the
CLI's own lock directory when it can be had (cooperating with every CLI whose gate is on), replace the file atomically
(a temp file in the same directory, renamed), then read it back before the spawn and retry a bounded number of times
if the record is gone; a record still lost at the spawn leaves the dialog standing for the human (viola types
nothing), and the start reads it as a modal. Whether the bound and this form are taken is the founder's (directive
item 3).

**The record — how the CLI writes it:** `ES(key)` → `{...config, projects: {...projects, [key]: {...projects[key] ??
ETe, hasTrustDialogAccepted: true}}}`, key `fD(cwd)` = the git root (canonical) or the cwd; `ETe`, a new project's
defaults: `allowedTools: []`, `mcpContextUris: []`, `mcpServers: {}`, `enabledMcpjsonServers: []`,
`disabledMcpjsonServers: []`, `hasTrustDialogAccepted: false`, `hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesApproved: false`,
`hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesWarningShown: false`. The CLI's own messages name the record as the user's remedy:
«…or set projects[<path>].hasTrustDialogAccepted: true in <config path>» (`Vj()` = the global config file).

**The record — how the CLI reads it (2.1.325 `SL()`; 2.1.326 `OU()`, the same body):** trusted when
`CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED`; else when this session already accepted; else when
`projects[<project key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted` is true, the project key `f0e()` = the cwd's git root when the cwd
is in a git repository, else the normalised cwd; else by a walk from the cwd up to the git root (`bS` → `SS`), any
folder on the way whose record is true trusting it — save a `rootOnly` branch (`M2o`: a root whose `Lzo(root)` is not
true) where only the root's record counts. **Unmeasured:** what `Lzo` decides (the `rootOnly` branch's condition).
The home folder's trust is never recorded (session-only).

6. No settings-schema key and no managed-settings field trusts a folder: the settings literals near the trust code
   are `additionalDirectories` (permission scope, no trust) and `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt` (bypass-mode
   prompt); the trust state lives only in the global config's `projects` map.
**→ No flag, setting, env key or managed field trusts a folder for an interactive session without doing more. The
ruling's second arm stands: the per-project trust record.**

5. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` / `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` / `--permission-mode` — permission
   bypass, no trust: not candidates.
4. `CLAUDE_CODE_IGNORE_PERSISTED_TRUST` / `--ignore-persisted-trust` — the opposite: no trust record counts.

3. `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED` (env) — the trust check returns trusted at once (`if(i.CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED)return!0`,
   2.1.325 `SL()`, 2.1.326 `OU()`), and BEYOND trust it switches off the project-permission gate (`wDo()` returns
   true → the gated project grants are not probed) and gives the `sandboxed` verdict to workspace checks: it is no
   trust flag but a sandbox posture — a widening of its own, named, not taken.

2. `--trusted-folder <absolute>` — «The current directory, which the host says a person trusted»: an option of the
   hidden `worktree-hook` subcommand (Claude Desktop's WorktreeCreate/Remove hooks) only → no flag arm.

1. `--trust-workspace` — «Trust the current folder for this run only, without asking (for scripts and CI)». Registered
   on the `ultrareview` subcommand only (2.1.325: the option chain after `--post` / `--no-post`; 2.1.326 the same, and
   the CLI's own `ultrareview … --no-post --trust-workspace --json` spawn); the self-hosted runner reads its own
   `--trust-workspace` / `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_TRUST_WORKSPACE` and SEEDS persisted trust by writing
   `projects[<path>] = {hasTrustDialogAccepted: true}` into `<configDir>/.claude.json` at mode 0600 (384). Not an

title: I1-phase-session-folder-directive.md.txt
body:
# Phase directive — «Session folder trusted by viola» (Epoch 4's head entry, viola-0.2.0, v2-33)

1. Scope is the route entry and its carry as they stand at `c2310c28`, nothing wider: a session viola starts in a
   folder the CLI never trusted opens with no trust dialog and no key typed by viola.
2. **The founder's ruling on HOW is in the carry, and its ORDER binds the phase:** FIRST measure whether the CLI has
   a flag or a setting that trusts a folder; if one exists, viola uses it. ONLY if none does, viola writes
   `projects[cwd].hasTrustDialogAccepted` into the user's `~/.claude.json`. So P3 measures before P4 chooses:
   - from the installed CLI itself, with no live start: its `--help` and every subcommand's, the settings schema
     and the strings of the 2.1.325 bundle (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude`) and of 2.1.326 —
     any flag, setting, environment key or managed-settings field that makes a folder trusted or skips the trust
     dialog; for each candidate say what it does BEYOND trust (a flag that also skips permission prompts is not a
     trust flag, and using it is a widening of its own — name it, do not take it);
   - what `projects[cwd]` holds beside `hasTrustDialogAccepted`, and which process writes that file when (measured
     2026-11-17: the host's other Claude sessions rewrite `~/.claude.json` about once a minute — a writer that
     reads, edits and writes it races them; say how the write is made so no other session's write is lost and
     none of ours is, or that it cannot be and what follows).
3. **Writing the CLI's own state file is a boundary widening, named so in the carry**, and takes its security-plan
   entry. The plan lists it as an Expected amendment; its exact bound (which key, which cwd, when, never another
   project's entry, what viola does when the file is absent, unreadable, a link, or not the JSON it expects, and
   that nothing of the file is logged) is put to the founder through the overseer at P3's end, in the block below
   — do not settle it yourself.
4. **SIZE and the live starts FIRST.** At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block:
   (a) what the measurement found — each candidate, what it does, and which arm of the ruling it selects;
   (b) whether the chunk fits one implement window (say your own window at that point), and a split named plainly
   if not — the placement is the founder's;
   (c) the live starts on the standing rig: for each the SHAPE first (the cwd and its trust state, what makes the
   dialog appear or not, what the start reads if the mechanism failed and the dialog DOES stand), then the exact
   count per CLI version (2.1.325 by path; PATH's 2.1.326 is unstamped — say whether this reading needs it), and
   **every byte the rig types, the STOP included**: the keys into a dialog or a box (granted anew per chunk) apart
   from the stop (Ctrl-C into the rig's own pty, or a no-key group kill — standing, per the re-worded
   `security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty`). The summary's `keys:` word names the argv grant only;
   the block names both.
   (d) what viola's write does to the founder's REAL config during a live start, if a start exercises it: the rig
   runs under a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so say which file the product writes there and that his real file is
   read only by the mark witness.
   The cap, the keys and the bound of item 3 are the founder's; the overseer brings them to him in one dialog.
   Plan every other step on the fake agent meanwhile.
5. No mutation run. Name each control's `--timeout S` in the plan's prose AND fire it with that flag, on an entry
   whose build reaches every binary its case needs; a control id — and a sweep pattern id — stays within 16
   characters; «holds» = those cases ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Every acceptance predicate is one that
   CAN fail: for each control say what the subject does when the guard is gone, measured or marked unmeasured.
6. A change to the fake agent's screens puts `cli_verify` in the gate block. A test that waits takes a bound under
   the 20 s lint. A gate entry that names an installed tool's path is checked against the host before the card.
7. A fold is decided at the PHASE. If implement meets a red that moves a plan entry it stops and says so BEFORE the
   operator pass.
8. A fork that is the founder's (a boundary widening, a live cap, a typed key, a placement) is asked through the
   overseer, who brings it to him by dialog — he is present, slow to answer; a technical fork is answered by relay
   at once.
9. Set NO scheduled wake or timer of your own. End every process you start.
10. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; rows read whole or by search; whether EVERY cited row is in
    the union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` /
    `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.
